meta.notes: [bulk-tag pass: added `ai-900` tag to 20 questions] [recall sweep: 1 balanced rewrites] [hardening pass: rebalanced answer positions to 5/5/5/5, removed give-away distractors in Q005, parallel option phrasing, consistent descriptors]

questions.question: Your team needs a single managed Azure workspace that lets data scientists train and deploy models with notebooks and the Python SDK, while business analysts use a no-code drag-and-drop designer. Which service fits best?
options: Azure AI Search (vector and keyword search)
questions.explanation: Azure Machine Learning is the end-to-end managed ML platform on Azure. It provides Automated ML, the visual Designer, hosted notebooks, the Python/CLI v2 SDK, MLOps pipelines, managed endpoints and a model registry. Databricks is a Spark analytics platform, Synapse is a unified analytics/data-warehouse service, and AI Search powers retrieval scenarios.

questions.question: A developer wants to add vision, language, speech and decision features to an app by calling pre-built REST endpoints without training any model. Which family of Azure services should they use?
questions.explanation: Azure AI services (formerly known as Cognitive Services) are pre-built, consumable AI APIs grouped into Vision, Language, Speech and Decision categories. Data Factory is for data movement, Logic Apps for workflow integration, and HDInsight for managed big-data clusters.

questions.question: Which type of machine learning is used to predict a continuous numeric value, such as the future selling price of a house from its features?
questions.explanation: Regression is a supervised learning technique that predicts a continuous numeric value (price, temperature, demand). Classification predicts a discrete category, clustering groups unlabeled data, and reinforcement learning learns through rewards from an environment.

questions.question: An online retailer wants to automatically segment shoppers by purchase behaviour when no category labels are available. Which machine-learning approach is appropriate?
options: Anomaly detection on streaming sensor data
questions.explanation: Clustering is an unsupervised technique that groups items by feature similarity when no labels are provided; k-means and DBSCAN are common implementations. Classification and regression need labeled training data, and anomaly detection looks for rare outliers rather than producing groupings.

questions.question: Microsoft publishes six guiding principles for Responsible AI that every team building AI services on Azure should adopt. They cover treating users fairly, building robust and safe products, understanding model decisions, respecting privacy, being inclusive, and assigning human accountability. Which list uses the exact wording of those six principles?
options: Fairness; reliability and safety; privacy and security; inclusiveness; transparency; accountability
Fairness; explainability; privacy and security; sustainability; transparency; human oversight and accountability
Reliability and safety; scalability; data minimisation; inclusiveness; interpretability; governance
Fairness; reliability and safety; confidentiality; inclusiveness; transparency; auditability
questions.explanation: Microsoft's six Responsible AI principles, in the exact wording Microsoft uses, are: Fairness; Reliability and Safety; Privacy and Security; Inclusiveness; Transparency; and Accountability. The other lists look close but each substitutes terms Microsoft does not use — 'explainability' or 'interpretability' in place of Transparency; 'human oversight', 'governance' or 'auditability' in place of Accountability; and extras such as sustainability, scalability, data minimisation or confidentiality that belong to other governance frameworks. Knowing the precise terms (Transparency, not explainability; Accountability, not auditability) is what the question tests.

questions.question: Your application needs to detect human faces in images and analyse attributes such as head pose, with some features requiring an approved Limited Access application. Which Azure AI service is purpose-built for this?
options: Azure AI Document Intelligence (forms and documents)
questions.explanation: Azure AI Face provides face detection, identification and attribute analysis. Several attributes (emotion, gender, age, makeup) are gated by the Limited Access programme and require an approved application. Vision Image Analysis covers general computer vision, Document Intelligence handles forms, and Speech handles audio.

questions.question: Your finance team needs to pull structured fields, tables and key-value pairs out of invoices and receipts using both pre-built and custom-trained models. Which Azure service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Azure AI Document Intelligence (formerly Form Recognizer) extracts text, key-value pairs, tables and structured fields from documents using pre-built models (invoices, receipts, IDs, business cards) or models you train. Content Safety filters harmful text, Translator handles machine translation, and Personalizer is a decision service for content ranking.

questions.question: Which feature inside Azure AI Language scores the overall opinion in a passage of text as positive, neutral or negative with a confidence value?
options: Named entity recognition (NER), which extracts opinion holders and targets from text for sentiment scoring
questions.explanation: Sentiment analysis classifies a piece of text as positive, neutral or negative and returns a confidence score; the same feature also supports per-aspect (opinion mining) scoring. Key phrase extraction surfaces the main concepts, NER finds entities such as people, places and dates, and language detection identifies the language.

questions.question: A call-centre app must transcribe live customer audio into text in real time. Which Azure AI Speech capability provides this?
questions.explanation: Speech to text converts spoken audio into written text in real time or from recorded files. Text to speech is the inverse (synthesising audio), Speech translation translates spoken input across languages, and Speaker recognition identifies or verifies a person by their voice.

questions.question: Your team wants to build a chatbot that answers user questions from an existing collection of FAQs, product documents and support URLs. Which Azure capability is designed for that?
options: Azure AI Metrics Advisor (business KPI monitoring)
Azure AI Language question answering (QnA service)
questions.explanation: The question answering feature of Azure AI Language (the successor to QnA Maker) builds a knowledge base from documents, URLs and FAQs and serves natural-language answers, often combined with Azure AI Bot Service. Personalizer ranks content, Metrics Advisor monitors KPI streams, and Anomaly Detector flags time-series outliers.

questions.question: A factory wants to flag unusual spikes in equipment-sensor time-series streams without having to train a model. Which Azure AI service is the right fit?
options: Azure AI Translator (machine translation), which converts time-series text between languages using neural models without labelled series data
questions.explanation: Azure AI Anomaly Detector is a pre-built decision service that finds anomalies in univariate or multivariate time-series data with little or no ML expertise. The other services handle machine translation, custom image classification and harmful-content filtering.

questions.question: You want to train an image classifier from a small set of labelled photos using a web portal that requires no code. Which Azure AI service is purpose-built for this?
options: Azure AI Face (face detection and analysis), which uses a browser portal to train custom vision models on portrait photos
Azure AI Vision (prebuilt Image Analysis API)
Azure AI Custom Vision (browser training portal)
Azure AI Video Indexer (video content insights)
questions.explanation: Azure AI Custom Vision (customvision.ai) lets you upload images, tag them, and train a custom image-classification or object-detection model through a browser portal, then export or call it via REST. Image Analysis offers prebuilt tags only, Video Indexer focuses on video, and Face is dedicated to faces.

questions.question: Which Azure Machine Learning feature iterates through algorithms, featurisation and hyperparameters to surface a high-quality model with minimal coding?
options: Azure ML Designer (drag-and-drop), which automates machine learning across algorithms and hyperparameters for classification tasks
questions.explanation: Automated ML (AutoML) iterates through algorithms, featurisation and hyperparameters to produce a leaderboard of models for classification, regression, forecasting, NLP and computer-vision tasks. Hyperdrive tunes a single training script, MLflow logs runs and artefacts, and the Designer is a drag-and-drop pipeline builder.

questions.question: When a team ships interpretability tooling that explains why a model produced a given prediction, which Microsoft Responsible AI principle is MOST directly supported?
questions.explanation: Transparency means people can understand how the AI system works and the basis of its decisions; interpretability tools such as SHAP and the Responsible AI dashboard in Azure ML support this principle. Accountability covers governance and human ownership of outcomes, Inclusiveness focuses on serving diverse users, and Reliability and Safety deals with consistent, safe operation — none of which is specifically about explaining individual predictions.

questions.question: An enterprise wants to use OpenAI GPT models inside Azure with regional hosting, private networking, content filters and Microsoft enterprise agreements. Which service should they choose?
options: Azure AI Language (NLP features), which provides access to OpenAI GPT models with Azure enterprise networking and regional hosting
questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI Service provides access to OpenAI's GPT, embeddings, DALL-E and Whisper models hosted on Azure with enterprise-grade security, regional availability, content filtering and integration with Azure networking and identity. AI Language covers NLP features, AI Search is a retrieval service, and Bot Service is a conversational framework.

questions.question: Which pattern grounds a generative AI model in current private knowledge by fetching relevant passages at inference time and passing them into the prompt, instead of changing the model weights?
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves the most relevant passages (often via vector search in Azure AI Search) and injects them into the prompt so the model answers using current, private content. Fine-tuning changes the weights themselves, RLHF aligns model behaviour through human preference data, and prompt compression simply reduces token usage.

questions.question: Which Azure AI service offers content filters that flag hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content in text and images, and is integrated with Azure OpenAI?
questions.explanation: Azure AI Content Safety analyses text and images for harmful categories (hate, violence, self-harm, sexual) with severity levels and supports Prompt Shield and protected-material detection for generative AI scenarios. Personalizer ranks content, Purview governs data, and Translator does machine translation.

questions.question: Which Azure service is the natural choice to implement knowledge mining: indexing a large set of documents and enriching them with AI skills (OCR, key phrases, entities) so users can search them?
options: Azure Data Lake Storage (file storage), which supports knowledge mining via AI Search skillsets with OCR and key phrase indexing
Azure AI Document Intelligence (forms and documents)
questions.explanation: Azure AI Search (formerly Cognitive Search) is the knowledge-mining service: it ingests documents from data sources, applies AI skills (OCR, key phrases, entities, vectors) and exposes a queryable index. It is also the typical retriever in RAG patterns. Data Lake stores files, Cosmos DB is a NoSQL database, and Document Intelligence extracts fields from individual forms.

questions.question: A model scores very high on its training data but performs poorly on new, unseen samples. What is this behaviour called?
questions.explanation: Overfitting means the model has memorised the training data, including its noise, and fails to generalise to new examples. Mitigations include collecting more data, regularisation, simpler models, cross-validation and early stopping. Underfitting is the opposite (model too simple), class imbalance is about skewed label distribution, and data drift is a change in input distribution after deployment.

questions.question: On a strongly imbalanced binary-classification problem such as credit-card fraud detection, which metric gives the most informative view of model quality?
questions.explanation: On imbalanced datasets, plain accuracy is misleading because predicting only the majority class still yields a high score. F1-score (the harmonic mean of precision and recall) — or precision/recall and AUC-PR — gives a much better picture. MAE and R-squared are regression metrics and do not apply to a classification task.
